problem: End-to-end RL agents for object-goal navigation from egocentric RGB, such as SAVN and Scene Prior, feed global CNN or graph features to the policy. Standard visual and transformer (MHA) attention averages over image regions and so discards where relevant objects and cues are, which weakens the spatial reasoning needed to steer toward a target.
motivation: Humans look for a target by attending to semantically related cues and their location, e.g. looking at the fridge when searching for a toaster. The authors argue that navigation needs both the 'what' (semantics) and the 'where' (spatial location) of observed objects. They propose that a spatially preserved attention distribution over image sub-windows, conditioned on the target, the last action and memory, can orient the agent and also make its decisions interpretable.
key_idea: Multiply ResNet18 spatial feature maps element-wise by a fused attention probability map over sub-windows, built from target (GloVe), last-action and LSTM-memory attentions whose fusion exponents are predicted per step from the LSTM state, and feed this spatially attended embedding to a SAVN meta-RL policy.
insight: Keeping the spatial layout of the attended features (p ⊙ v rather than an attention-weighted average) is what matters. Replacing the module with transformer multi-head attention drops SR from 46.20 to 30.70 and SPL from 17.88 to 9.80, below SAVN's 40.86 / 16.15. Target attention is the dominant cue: removing it gives SR 29.60 / SPL 9.41. The action and memory units mainly help path efficiency: without memory, SR stays at 45.6 but SPL drops to 15.39; without action attention, SR is 41.00 and SPL 14.41. Learned, state-dependent fusion weights β matter too: fixing β=1 gives SR 38.80. The product-of-experts fusion is also far more parameter-efficient than concatenating the three attended maps (7.5M vs 20.4M parameters) and is 22% better in success and 31% better in SPL.
method: Visual encoder: ImageNet-pretrained ResNet18 topmost conv map (n_v×n_v×d_v); each spatial cell v_ij is treated as an image sub-window.
Target attention: cosine similarity between W_v·v_ij and W_g·GloVe(target word), softmaxed over the n_v×n_v cells to give p_g.
Action attention: cosine similarity between W_v·v_ij and W_a·(previous-step action distribution), softmaxed to give p_a; this biases attention toward the direction the agent is turning or moving.
Memory attention: cosine similarity between W_v·v_ij and W_m·(LSTM hidden state at t-1), softmaxed to give p_m; this summarises what was already seen in the episode.
Fused attention: p ∝ p_g^{β_g} · p_a^{β_a} · p_m^{β_m}, where the β weights are real-valued functions of the LSTM state and are learned per time step.
Attended embedding: element-wise multiplication p(i,j)·v_ij keeps the spatial dimension and near-zeroes irrelevant cells; the result is input to the LSTM and actor-critic.

Policy learning: SAVN framework (MAML-style test-time adaptation via a learned interaction loss) trained with actor-critic, 12 synchronous agents (A2C) as well as an A3C variant; reward +5 for success and -0.01 per step.

setting.backbone: ImageNet-pretrained ResNet18 features + GloVe target embedding + attention module + LSTM actor-critic (SAVN meta-RL), trained with A2C
setting.model_size: 7.5M parameters (stated for the fused-attention system vs 20.4M for the concatenation baseline)
setting.training_data: RL in AI2-THOR on the SAVN split: 20 training scenes per room type × 4 room types (kitchen, living room, bedroom, bathroom) = 80 training scenes; 5/5 validation/test scenes per type
setting.observation: egocentric RGB + target object class word (GloVe)
setting.privileged: none in the main setting. The extra experiment in the Du et al. setting uses simulator-provided object detections.

numbers.extra: 1000 test episodes (250 per room type); success = Done within 1 m with target visible; max 200 steps living room / 100 steps other rooms; model selected on validation success

The concatenation-fusion comparison is likewise given only as relative percentages.
results: On the AI2-THOR SAVN test set (1000 episodes), the A2C model reaches SR 46.20 / SPL 17.88, and 32.63 / 15.94 on episodes with L≥5. This beats SAVN (40.86 / 16.15; 28.70 / 13.91) and Scene Prior (35.13 / 15.47). The A3C variant (43.20 / 16.99) also beats SAVN's A3C learner. When the attention module is added on top of Du et al.'s detection-based architecture, it improves SR by 9.2% and SPL by 9.1% relative.
limitations: Evaluated only in small single-room AI2-THOR scenes (SAVN split) with RGB only. Absolute SPL remains low (~18), and there is no multi-room or real-robot evaluation.

Failure cases include misclassifying visually similar objects (a bathtub taken for a sink) and missing partially occluded targets (a box under a table). No depth input is used, so distance estimation is imprecise.
Gains are within the SAVN meta-RL framework, and the paper notes result instability across platforms and GPUs with asynchronous training.
compares_to: Du et al. 2020 (object relation / detection-based navigation)
